news.headline: Emotional Greg Schiano authors 'special' win, Rutgers' first at PSU since 1988
news.description: Less than two weeks removed from Rutgers announcing embattled Greg Schiano would return as coach for a 19th season, the Scarlet Knights stunned Penn State 25-24 Saturday, their first win over the Nittany Lions since 1988, and just their third this year.

news.headline: Notre Dame loses safety Luke Talich to injury in first quarter vs. SMU
news.description: Notre Dame starting safety Luke Talich left the Fighting Irish's game against SMU in the first quarter with an apparent right leg injury suffered on the opening drive of the game Saturday night in South Bend, Indiana.

news.headline: Brandon's two TD runs lift No. 9 Tennessee past LSU
news.description: Tennessee's stifling defense shut down LSU, and the No. 9 Volunteers beat the Tigers 27-13 on Saturday to maintain their place in the College Football Playoff hunt.

news.headline: Bryce Underwood makes most of second chance, sparks Michigan's upset of UCLA
news.description: Reinserted as Michigan's starting quarterback earlier this week, Bryce Underwood threw a 3-yard 2-point conversion pass Jalen Hoffman, lifting the Wolverines to an 18-16 triple-overtime win over previously unbeaten No. 4 UCLA on Saturday night.

news.headline: Nebraska's jab at Ohio State's 'THE' leads top Week 12 CFB trolls
news.description: Nebraska deployed a simple but effective troll that poked fun at its opponent's propensity to emphasize the "the" in "The Ohio State University."

news.headline: Indiana's CFP hopes take hit after OT loss at Washington
news.description: Indiana might not get a chance to defend its national championship after losing 27-24 at Washington on Saturday.

news.headline: UCLA loses Ty Dieffenbach to injury, stays resolute with B1G title game in reach
news.description: UCLA coach Bob Chesney said his message to the Bruins was, "Nobody hang your head," despite losing QB Ty Dieffenbach to injury in a tough, 18-16 defeat at Michigan on Saturday.

news.headline: Preseason No. 1 Ohio State suffers fourth loss, will 'evaluate what's going on'
news.description: For coach Ryan Day and his Ohio State Buckeyes, the dream of a College Football Playoff run is dead, as the preseason No. 1 team in college football lost its fourth game on Saturday afternoon, a 31-28 decision at the hands of the Nebraska Cornhuskers.

wiki.title: Jalen Mayo
wiki.intro: Jalen Mayo is an American college football cornerback for the Houston Cougars. He previously played for the Virginia Union Panthers and the Stephen F. Austin Lumberjacks.

sections.title: Early life
sections.text:
Mayo attended Phoebus High School in Hampton, Virginia, where he excelled in football as a wide receiver and defensive back. As a senior in 2021, he earned first-team all-state honors at both positions after tallying 34 receptions for 585 yards and seven touchdowns on offense and seven interceptions and 15 pass breakups on defense. Mayo helped the Phantoms compile a 14–1 record and win the Virginia High School League (VHSL) Class 3 state championship. Mayo returned two interceptions for touchdowns in a 28–7 win over the defending state champions, Hopewell High School, in the regional playoffs. In the state title game the next month, he caught a touchdown in the first quarter before notching an interception in the final minute of a 22–14 win over Liberty Christian Academy, securing the school's eighth state championship in 20 years.
Mayo was an unrated recruit. He received just one college offer from Virginia Union University, a school located about 30 minutes from his home in Hampton with an Division II football program, and signed to play for the Panthers on National Signing Day in February 2022.

sections.title: College career
sections.text:
As a freshman in 2022, Mayo took a redshirt after suffering an ankle injury and did not play any games. In 2023, he registered 20 tackles, two tackles for loss, three interceptions, and three pass breakups, earning Central Intercollegiate Athletic Association (CIAA) all-rookie accolades. In 2024, Mayo recorded 52 tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss, three interceptions, one forced fumble, and seven pass breakups. He also helped the Panthers win back-to-back CIAA titles.
Mayo transferred to Stephen F. Austin State University to play for the Lumberjacks. In 2025, he posted 48 tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss, four interceptions, nine pass breakups, and one forced fumble, helping the Lumberjacks win the Southland Conference title. Mayo earned first-team all-Southland honors, and was named a second-team FCS All-American by multiple publications. He entered the NCAA transfer portal after the season and was rated as the No. 9 and No. 27 cornerback in the portal by Rivals.com and 247Sports, respectively.
Mayo transferred to the University of Houston during the January 2026 transfer window to play for the Cougars, following his former cornerbacks coach Marcus Trice, who had been hired in the same role with the Cougars a few weeks prior. After a strong performances in the spring and fall camps, Mayo was named a starter at cornerback heading into the 2026 season.
